newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan covered on corn, eyes lower soybean prices.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan covered on corn, eyes lower soybean prices.

text.p: Taiwan's corn buyers, hurt by the recent sharp fall in Chicago futures are likely to stay out of the market this week, but soybean buyers may place tenders due to low U.S. and South American basis prices, traders said on Monday.
"Corn buyers are already well covered through July and so the recent sharp decline in Chicago corn futures is not good for them," one corn trader said.
"Corn buyers are likely to stay sidelined and wait for corn futures to settle down, he said.
Taiwan's soybean buyers are also well covered until July, but better-than-expected results in recent tenders may lure some to cover their needs after July, a trader said.
"Soybean buyers like the prices they got in recent tenders and may return to the market for later shipments," he said.

Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought two 54,000-tonne shipments at 40.38 U.S. cents a tonne over Chicago futures in recent tenders -- surprisingly below earlier U.S. Gulf basis premiums, which had been about 80 U.S. cents.
Taiwan's wheat buyers are not expected in the market this week.
Local Pacific Northwest freight cost were at about US$11.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico ranged from $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized June shipments.
